mva.lead: Bring sales records, VAT codes and reconciliations together before preparing your Norwegian VAT return.
tasks: Review your sales channels
We look at what you sell and where it is recorded, especially when invoices, point-of-sale transactions and online payments pass through different systems.
Check records and codes
We identify purchases and sales that need a closer look and agree how to collect missing documents and handle credit notes.
Prepare for filing
We reconcile the return against the bookkeeping and agree who will review, approve and file it.
mva.exampleTitle: The store payout is lower than the sales total
mva.example: A single payout can bundle purchases, refunds and fees. The payment provider’s report helps us explain the difference and spot entries that need checking.
prepare: List your sales channels and say whether you’re registered for Norwegian VAT.
Find one sales report and a sample payout report. We’ll agree how to share them securely if needed.
faq: Can you work with our existing setup?
Yes. We start by checking how you record purchases and sales today and what needs to change.
What if I’m unsure about an invoice from abroad?
Tell us what the invoice covers and where the supplier is based. We’ll review the details before assessing how to record it.

arsoppgjor.lead: Get help closing the books, resolving outstanding items and working out what needs to be filed for your business.
tasks: Review what’s left
We check your business structure, period and the work already done. Then we agree on the outstanding items and reports.
Reconcile balance sheet items
Depending on the business, we can review bank balances, unpaid invoices, loans, inventory and business equipment.
Prepare for review
We explain major figures and identify what needs approval. We clarify responsibilities with you, the board and any auditor.
arsoppgjor.exampleTitle: A December invoice arrives in January
arsoppgjor.example: We check what the invoice covers, which period the expense relates to and whether it has already been included in the close.
prepare: Find the latest trial balance and list major changes during the year.
Make a note of any inventory counts, loan statements or invoices still to be checked.
faq: Can I ask for year-end help only?
We can assess that once we know how up-to-date the books are and what records are available.
What if our bookkeeping is unfinished?
We check what is missing and agree on any additional work before settling the scope.

radgivning.lead: Use your accounts to make the next decision, whether you’re starting a business, considering an investment or looking at cash flow.
tasks: Choose tools and routines
We look at how you invoice, accept payments and keep purchase records, then review options that fit your workflow.
Build a working budget
We use expected revenue, recurring costs and payment dates to identify which assumptions matter most.
Understand what drives the figures
We can review margins or the amount tied up in unpaid invoices when those figures matter to the decision you’re making.
radgivning.exampleTitle: Is this the right time for a large investment?
radgivning.example: We can compare two purchase dates and see how cash might change if sales are lower or customers pay later than planned.
prepare: Write down the decision you need to make and when.
Bring rough estimates for the price, income and payment dates if available.
faq: Can we start with one question?
Yes. We can focus the first conversation on one decision and see if further work makes sense.
Can I talk to you before starting a business?
Yes. Tell us what you plan to sell, how customers will pay and whether you expect to employ anyone.

servering.lead: Bring daily sales reports, card payouts and payroll records into a routine that fits a busy venue.
tasks: Match takings and deposits
We compare till and card terminal reports with bank deposits and tie delayed payouts back to their sales.
Track delivery platform settlements
We look at how orders, discounts, refunds and fees show up so you can separate sales from cash deposited.
Gather payroll inputs
We agree on who approves hours, allowances and other payroll details before each pay run.
servering.exampleTitle: A busy Saturday shows up in the bank on Tuesday
servering.example: The till and terminal reports give us a way to match that later deposit and spot any difference worth investigating.
prepare: List your tills, payment providers and ordering platforms.
Tell us who closes the till and how timesheets are approved.
faq: Can we keep our till system?
We start with the reports from your current system and check whether they give us the information we need.
How will you follow up a mismatch?
We identify the settlement and tell you which report or explanation is missing.

handverk.lead: Track time, materials and invoices when several jobs are running at once.
tasks: Assign costs to each job
We help you label purchases and supplier invoices by project so you can follow material and subcontractor costs.
Collect approved hours
We review who logs and approves hours so the same records can support payroll and project reporting.
Follow the invoicing schedule
We agree how changes, completion stages and invoice dates are recorded and checked.
handverk.exampleTitle: One supplier invoice covers two sites
handverk.example: If purchases carry a project reference, we can split the costs before reporting. This makes it easier to see which job is using more of its budget.
prepare: Describe how you track hours, purchases and additional work.
Pick a typical job to use as an example.
faq: Do we have to change software?
We look at what your existing tools can do first. You may just need a clearer routine.
Can we track small jobs too?
Yes. We can adapt the level of detail to the information you actually use.

netthandel.lead: Connect orders, fees, refunds and payouts so you can follow sales across channels.
tasks: Map the payment flow
We identify where people buy, which providers handle payment and when the money reaches your bank.
Reconcile settlement reports
We compare sales with refunds, cancellations, shipping and fees to explain why a payout differs from gross sales.
Review stock and records
We look at what reports are available for purchases, inventory and any overseas sales, then agree on checks that fit the business.
netthandel.exampleTitle: A return appears in a different month from the order
netthandel.example: The order reference and settlement report help us tie the refund to the original sale without relying on the bank entry alone.
prepare: List your shops, marketplaces and payment providers.
Find a report showing sales, refunds and fees together.
faq: Can you work with several shops?
We can assess that after seeing each shop’s reports and how they reach your bookkeeping.
What about selling abroad?
Tell us where customers are based and how goods are shipped. We’ll identify which records and VAT questions to look at.

konsulent.lead: Keep track of billable time, client expenses and payments without taking too much time away from client work.
tasks: Turn work into invoices
We trace hours, project milestones or fixed fees to invoices and agree on who approves and checks each step.
Record project expenses
We review how travel, purchases and subscriptions are documented, and how you identify expenses to recharge.
Plan for uneven income
We can use expected payment dates and regular costs to plan for quieter periods between projects.
konsulent.exampleTitle: The work is finished but the final invoice is outstanding
konsulent.example: A quick comparison of completed milestones and invoices shows what is still due to be billed and gives you a clearer cash forecast.
prepare: Describe how you charge clients and how often you invoice.
Note which costs you tend to pay on a client’s behalf.
faq: Can you help a sole proprietor?
Yes. We agree on the scope based on your projects, billing routines and the tasks you want to keep.
Can I send the invoices myself?
Yes. We can agree who handles invoicing and how you’d like us to follow up payments.

transport.lead: Manage payments for jobs, payroll records and the costs of running your vehicles.
tasks: Check settlements against completed jobs
We look at how jobs turn into invoices and payouts, particularly if you work with several customers or platforms.
Track operating costs
We agree how to record fuel, tolls, leases and maintenance, for example by vehicle when that helps you manage the fleet.
Plan for a vehicle change
Identifying the largest recurring costs makes it easier to compare vehicles and estimate the cash impact of a replacement.
transport.exampleTitle: Which vehicle costs most to run?
transport.example: If records are tagged consistently, we can compare ongoing costs and see what explains the difference.
prepare: List your vehicles and how they’re financed.
Describe how you record jobs, wages and travel expenses.
faq: Can reporting be split by vehicle?
We review whether this is useful and whether the income and costs can be assigned consistently.
Can you help with bookkeeping and payroll?
Yes. We agree what help you need, what records are available and who approves them before payday.

eiendom.lead: Follow rental income, operating bills and maintenance across one or several units.
tasks: Match rent agreements with receipts
We use agreed rents and amendments to follow payments, arrears and any differences.
Assign costs to properties
We review how service charges, insurance and maintenance can be coded so you see which property they relate to.
Prepare for year-end
We review relevant agreements, loans and larger works so the items that need assessment are documented.
eiendom.exampleTitle: One maintenance job covers two units
eiendom.example: A clear description and a breakdown of the invoice make it easier to follow costs for each unit and explain the year-end figures.
prepare: List the properties or units you rent out and the kinds of leases you have.
Describe how you currently track rent and service charges.
faq: Can we get separate reports for each property?
We can assess this if the income and costs can be identified by property or unit.
What should I keep for a large refurbishment?
Keep itemised invoices and a description of the work. We can review which accounting points need to be resolved.
